incidents.title: Shai-Hulud npm worm: malicious bash script likely LLM-generated
incidents.targets: npm maintainers and packages, wide ecosystem
incidents.outcome: Self-replicating worm stole credentials and republished infected packages.
incidents.confidenceReason: Unit 42 assesses LLM use with moderate confidence from comments and emojis in the script.
incidents.summary: Unit 42 judged that the worm's bash payload was written with LLM help, based on stylistic artifacts. It framed the worm as following s1ngularity's weaponization of AI tools.
incidents.quote: Unit 42 also assesses with moderate confidence that an LLM was used to generate the malicious bash script, based on inclusion of comments and emojis.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

harness.note: AI used as assistant or tool, not as an agent harness

incidents.title: Cybercriminals exploit X's Grok AI to bypass ad protections and spread malware
incidents.outcome: Malicious links reached millions of feeds through Grok's replies.
incidents.confidenceReason: The only source is a Hacker News page whose fetched text is the headline plus boilerplate. No investigator wording is visible.
incidents.summary: Malvertisers hid links in video ads on X and tagged Grok asking where the video came from, so the trusted Grok account replied with the link, spreading it to fake CAPTCHA scams and infostealers.
incidents.quote: In the next step, the fraudsters tag Grok in replies to the post using a throwaway account, asking something similar to "where is this video from?," prompting the AI chatbot to visibly display the link in response.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only The Hacker News has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: Chinese state group ran largely autonomous espionage campaign via Claude Code
incidents.targets: About thirty targets: tech companies, financial institutions, chemical manufacturers, government agencies
incidents.outcome: A small number of intrusions succeeded; accounts banned.
incidents.confidenceReason: Anthropic detected and disrupted the campaign and reports its details.
incidents.summary: Operators built a framework that drove Claude Code through reconnaissance, exploitation, credential theft and exfiltration, with humans approving only a few decision points.
incidents.quote: the threat actor was able to use AI to perform 80-90% of the campaign, with human intervention required only sporadically

harness.note: Operators built a framework driving Claude Code through recon, exploitation and exfiltration

sources.title: Disrupting the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign

incidents.title: Criminals discuss weaponizing HexStrike AI against Citrix NetScaler zero-days
incidents.actor: Underground forum actors (later attributed in press to Storm-1575)
models: unspecified LLMs via HexStrike AI MCP server
incidents.outcome: Forum claims of exploitation and sale of compromised appliances; Check Point said it lacked proof of use in attacks at publication.
incidents.confidenceReason: Check Point reports underground discussion and claims, not confirmed attack telemetry; the Storm-1575 attribution appears only in later secondary coverage.
incidents.summary: Within hours of HexStrike AI's release, underground channels discussed using it against freshly disclosed Citrix zero-days. The framework connects LLMs to 150+ security tools through MCP.
incidents.quote: malicious actors began discussing how to weaponize it

harness.note: Open-source MCP framework linking LLMs to 150+ security tools; criminal use is forum discussion, not confirmed telemetry

sources.title: Hexstrike-AI: When LLMs Meet Zero-Day Exploitation

incidents.title: HONESTCUE malware outsourced stage-two code generation to Gemini
incidents.confidenceReason: The Gemini API call is certain, but GTIG frames it as experimentation: families 'that experiment with using Gemini's API'; 'likely in the proof-of-concept stage'; no victim. Scope question: method excludes PoC tools that never touched a victim.
incidents.summary: A downloader sent hard-coded prompts to the Gemini API and ran the returned C# to fetch and execute a second-stage payload.
incidents.quote: HONESTCUE is a downloader and launcher framework that sends a prompt via Google Gemini's API and receives C# source code as the response.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Google Threat Intelligence Group has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: First malicious MCP in the wild: the Postmark backdoor that's stealing your emails
incidents.outcome: Every email sent through the server by victims' AI assistants was copied to the attacker.
incidents.confidenceReason: Koi read the package code: 'Since version 1.0.16, it's been quietly copying every email to the developer's personal server'. The live page no longer carries the article; the archive copy does. The AI here is the victim's assistant running a poisoned tool, not AI doing the attacker's work.
incidents.summary: A trojanized postmark-mcp npm package, used by AI assistants to send email, silently BCC'd every outgoing message to an attacker-controlled address; Koi calls it the first malicious MCP server seen in the wild.
incidents.quote: We literally handed him the keys, said "here, run this code with full permissions," and let our AI assistants use it hundreds of times a day.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Koi Security has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.
